title: Microsoft Purview DLP: policy sync status within 30 minutes (Worldwide)
summary: The rollout windows, automatic default, device-status navigation and Graph operation are supported. Licensing should identify the published Endpoint DLP entitlement rather than remain unknown, and several supporting sources need citations; these are minor corrections.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance controls; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: The Endpoint DLP troubleshooting page says policy sync status in the devices list can take up to 2 hours to update.
claims.quote: It might take up to 2 hours for the status in the devices list to update.

claims.claim: The Endpoint DLP overview says policy updates generally take about an hour to synchronize across the service.
claims.quote: When a policy is updated in Microsoft Purview portal, it generally takes about an hour for those updates to be synchronized across the service.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Per-device policy sync status is available in Microsoft Purview portal at Settings > Device onboarding > Devices.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Settings (gear icon in the upper right corner) > Device onboarding > Devices.

claims.claim: POST /v1.0/security/runHuntingQuery is the Microsoft Graph operation for querying advanced hunting data.
claims.quote:
This method is for advanced hunting in Microsoft 365 Defender.
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/security/runHuntingQuery

claims.claim: The Graph request body specifies the hunting query through the Query property.
claims.quote: In the request body, provide a JSON object with the Query property, and optionally include the Timespan and workspaceId properties.

claims.claim: The DeviceInfo table's DlpInfo column provides the corresponding Endpoint DLP device configuration and policy synchronization data.
claims.quote: The JSON object can be used to query and report on device configuration status, policy synchronization status, Endpoint DLP enablement, and other configuration details for onboarded devices.

claims.claim: Viewing Policy sync status is a read-only observation, not a way to change enforcement timing.
claims.quote: The Policy sync status shows you if the device received the latest policy version, or if the corresponding policies synced successfully to the device.

claims.claim: The hunting operation reads data rather than modifying the DLP policy.
claims.quote: Queries a specified set of event, activity, or entity data supported by Microsoft 365 Defender to proactively look for specific threats in your environment.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Policy sync status indicates whether the device received the latest policy version.
claims.quote: The Policy sync status shows you if the device received the latest policy version, or if the corresponding policies synced successfully to the device.

claims.claim: The three policy sync status values are Updated, Not updated and Not available.
claims.quote:
Configuration status and the Policy sync status of all your onboarded devices have three possible values.
Updated
Not updated
Not available

claims.claim: Updated means the device successfully received the latest policy version.
claims.quote: If the status is Updated, the device successfully received the latest policy version.

claims.claim: Not updated indicates that the device has not synced the latest policy updates.
claims.quote: This device isn't synced the latest policy updates.

claims.claim: Devices must be online for policy updates to happen.
claims.quote: Devices must be online for the policy update to happen. If the status isn't updating, check the last time the device was seen.

claims.where: Scope; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: For a custom account viewing device management settings, Learn lists Compliance admin, Compliance data admin, Global reader, Security admin and Global admin Entra roles.
claims.quote:
If you want to use a custom account to view the device management settings, it must be in one of these roles:
Compliance admin
Compliance data admin
Global reader
Security admin
Global admin

claims.claim: Device management supports Entra roles, not Purview roles.
claims.quote: Device management currently only supports Entra roles. Purview roles are not supported.

claims.claim: DLP policy changes can be tested in simulation or audit mode before enforcement.
claims.quote: When you deploy a new policy or need to modify an existing one, you should run it in simulation mode, and then review the alerts to assess its accuracy.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/dlp-test-dlp-policies to sources for the advice to test policy changes before enforcement.

claims.claim: The documented interactive advanced hunting route uses the Microsoft Defender portal.
claims.quote:
Go to the Microsoft Defender portal
Navigate to Investigation & response > Hunting > Advanced hunting
Query the DeviceInfo table
Expand the DlpInfo column to view Endpoint DLP device details

claims.claim: The Graph hunting operation requires the permissions listed in its reference.
claims.quote:
Delegated (work or school account) | ThreatHunting.Read.All | ThreatHunting.ReadWrite.All
Application | ThreatHunting.Read.All | ThreatHunting.ReadWrite.All

claims.claim: The troubleshooting procedure directs administrators to the device details pane for remediation when policy sync status is Not updated.
claims.quote: If the status is Not updated or Not available, follow the remediation steps in the details pane and the steps in the workflow diagram.
